strategies.name: support_bounce_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: Let the first 5-15 minutes establish where support is, then enter long when price wicks down to a dynamic support level and bounces.
strategies.exit_summary: Ride the bounce up to resistance and take profit quickly on a small move; get in and get out, rinse and repeat.

entry_sequence.action: time your entries once you have allowed the first 5 to 15 minutes to pass because it allows you to establish where support is at
this candle wick came down bounced off of that and then the stock got a up move ... the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp
you get in here as support and you ride it to resistance and you exit

instrument_classification.instrument_note: Taught on stocks — speaker repeatedly says 'stock' and 'stock price' ("profiting from minor price changes in a stock price", "look at where stock is bottom at"); no specific ticker named, generic 5-minute intraday scalp.

coverage_notes: 13 EMA initial support variant — APPEARS (variants[0] + confluences[0]): 'this 13 EMA operated as a initial support So this candle wick came down bounced off of that and then the stock got a up move'.
200 EMA deeper support variant — APPEARS (variants[1]): 'this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status'.

demand-zone/price-action support variant — APPEARS (variants[2] + confluences[1..2]): 'look at Price action look at where stock is bottom at and bounce from' and 'spot the demand zones ... an area of emphasis for buyers to step in at which might be operating as support and or demand Zone'.

breakdown 'big move once support lost' — ABSENT-WITH-REASON: the speaker mentions it ('we finally lost the support level here and then this is the big move you guys really want to learn to catch') but does not teach a runnable long support-bounce entry for it — the words are self-contradictory as an entry ('you want to exit right there' then 'you would have entered there ... you had that coming all the way down'), and it describes catching a post-breakdown down-move, which is the opposite direction from this long support-bounce scalp. No runnable entry for THIS strategy, so it is not extracted as a variant.

stop = null — GENUINE ABSENCE: speaker repeats risk discipline ('managing your risk getting in getting out not overstaying your welcome') but never states a stop-loss level or a rule for where to place a stop.

Exit is target-bearing, not purely gestural: speaker gives concrete-ish targets (resistance; a few green candles; 10/15/30/50 cent moves), so gestural_exit=false even though no exact stop/target price is given.
